author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Set full or limited RGB range on an external display
summary: Use near-black and near-white reference steps to identify a range mismatch between Android, an adapter, receiver, and television; change one device at a time and preserve the input preset that shows every legal level.
heroAlt: Official PCSX2 capture with dark shadows and bright highlights suitable for checking display-range clipping

blocks.text: Test code values instead of judging one game scene

A full/limited mismatch can make black look gray or crush several dark steps into one, while the opposite end may clip highlight detail. The emulator frame, Android compositor, USB-C or HDMI adapter, receiver, and television input can each influence the signal. Begin with a reference containing distinct near-black and near-white steps, then use a game scene only as a real-world confirmation.
Brightness and contrast controls can partially disguise a range mismatch. Record them, return the display to a neutral input preset, and solve signal interpretation before artistic picture tuning.

items: A test image containing labeled near-black and near-white steps.
The exact phone, adapter, receiver, cable path, and television input recorded.
HDR, dynamic contrast, black enhancer, and power-saving picture changes disabled.
A pixel-accurate or no-overscan display mode.
A dark game checkpoint with a bright light or sky in the same frame.

blocks.text: Find the component that interprets the range incorrectly

items: 1. Display the reference locally on the phone and record which steps are distinguishable.
2. Connect the external chain and choose the television input preset without custom brightness compensation.
3. Inspect the darkest labeled steps; gray black suggests full values interpreted as limited, while merged dark steps can indicate the reverse or excessive black level.
4. Inspect the brightest steps independently for clipping.
5. Change the source or television range control once, never both simultaneously, and repeat the complete step count.
6. Bypass the receiver or alternate the adapter when the endpoints cannot agree.
7. Disable HDR conversion for the SDR baseline, then test HDR as a separate pipeline if required.
8. Confirm the accepted chain in the dark game checkpoint and store settings per physical input.

blocks.text: Range describes how numeric signal values map to black and white. When source and sink assume different mappings, calibration sliders cannot restore values already clipped or expand a compressed signal without side effects. Step patterns expose both endpoints more reliably than a cinematic frame whose intended grade is unknown.
The chain passes only when shadow and highlight structure coexist.

items: All intended near-black steps remain individually visible.
Near-white steps are distinct without tint or posterization.
Black is not elevated to gray under the neutral preset.
The game checkpoint preserves dark textures and bright sky detail together.
Reconnect and cold-start the chain without silently changing the input mode.

blocks.text: Range symptoms that point to another stage

items: The direct phone capture is already clipped: inspect emulator shader and Android color transforms.
Only HDR loses steps: keep SDR accepted and diagnose tone mapping separately.
Bypassing the receiver fixes the pattern: correct or replace that link.
Different television inputs behave differently: preserve independent presets rather than copying values.

blocks.text: Restore the documented neutral input preset

Return source and television range to their recorded automatic or baseline modes, restore neutral brightness and contrast, disable experimental HDR conversion, and reconnect the original chain. Keep the failing step counts beside the accepted configuration.
Screenshots cannot prove the HDMI signal

A direct Android screenshot is useful before the connector, but it cannot reveal how an adapter or television decodes the outgoing signal. Photographing the panel can document the chain, although camera exposure must remain locked.
